source_text: Καὶ ὁ Τρύφων· Ἐμοὶ μὲν δοκοῦσιν, εἶπεν, οἱ λέγοντες ἄνθρωπον γεγονέναι αὐτὸν καὶ κατ᾿ ἐκλογὴν κεχρῖσθαι καὶ Χριστὸν γεγονέναι πιθανώτερον ὑμῶν λέγειν, τῶν ταῦτα ἅπερ φῂς λεγόντων· καὶ γὰρ πάντες ἡμεῖς τὸν Χριστὸν ἄνθρωπον ἐξ ἀνθρώπων προσδοκῶμεν γενήσεσθαι , καὶ τὸν Ἡλίαν χρῖσαι αὐτὸν ἐλθόντα. Ἐὰν δὲ οὗτος φαίνηται ὢν ὁ Χριστός, ἄνθρωπον μὲν ἐξ ἀνθρώπων γενόμενον ἐκ παντὸς ἐπίστασθαι δεῖ. Ἐκ δὲ τοῦ μηδὲ Ἡλίαν ἐληλυθέναι οὐδὲ τοῦτον ἀποφαίνομαι εἶναι. Κἀγὼ πάλιν ἐπυθόμην αὐτοῦ· Οὐχὶ Ἡλίαν φησὶν ὁ λόγος διὰ Ζαχαρίου ἐλεύσεσθαι πρὸ τῆς ἡμέρας τῆς μεγάλης καὶ φοβερᾶς ταύτης τοῦ κυρίου ; Κἀκεῖνος ἀπεκρίνατο· Μάλιστα. Ἐὰν οὖν ὁ λόγος ἀναγκάζῃ ὁμολογεῖν ὅτι δύο παρουσίαι τοῦ Χριστοῦ προεφητεύοντο γενησόμεναι, μία μέν. ἐν ᾖ παθητός καὶ ἄτιμος καὶ ἀειδὴς φανήσεται , ἡ δὲ ἑτέρα, ἐν ᾗ καὶ ἔνδοξος καὶ κριτὴς ἁπάντων ἐλεύσεται , ὡς καὶ ἐν πολλοῖς τοῖς προλελεγμένοις ἀποδέδεικται, οὐχὶ τῆς φοβερᾶς καὶ μεγάλης ἡμέρας τουτέστι τῆς δευτέρας παρουσίας αὐτοῦ, πρόοδον γενήσεσθαι τὸν Ἡλίαν νοήσομεν τὸν λόγον τοῦ θεοῦ κεκηρυχέναι; Μάλιστα, ἀπεκρίνατο. Καὶ ὁ ἡμέτερος οὖν κύριος, ἔφην, τοῦτο αὐτὸ ἐν τοῖς διδάγμασιν αὐτοῦ παρέδωκε γενησόμενον, εἰπὼν καὶ Ἡλίαν ἐλεύσεσθαι · καὶ ἡμεῖς τοῦτο ἐπιστάμεθα γενησόμενον, ὅταν μέλλῃ ἐν δόξῃ ἐξ οὐρανῶν παραγίνεσθαι ὁ ἡμέτερος κύριος Ἰησοῦς Χριστός, οὗ καὶ τῆς πρώτης φανερώσεως κῆρυξ προῆλθε τὸ ἐν Ἡλίᾳ γενόμενον πνεῦμα τοῦ θεοῦ, ἐν Ἰωάννῃ , τῷ γενομένῳ ἐν τῷ γένει ὑμῶν προφήτῃ, μεθ᾿ ὃν οὐδεὶς ἕτερος λοιπὸν παρ᾿ ὑμῖν ἐφάνη προφήτης· ὅστις ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰορδάνην ποταμὸν καθεζόμενος ἐβόα· Ἐγὼ μὲν ὑμᾶς βαπτίζω ὲν ὕδατι εἰς μετάνοιαν· ἥξει δὲ ὁ ἰσχυρότερός μου, οὗ οὐκ εἰμὶ ἱκανὸς τὰ ὑποδήματα βαστάσαι· αὐτὸς ὑμᾶς βαπτίσει ἐν πνεύματι ἁγίῳ καὶ πυρί. Οὗ τὸ πτύον αὐτοῦ ἐν τῇ χειρὶ αὐτοῦ, καὶ διακαθαριεῖ τὴν ἅλωνα αὐτοῦ καὶ τὸν σῖτον συνάξει εἰς τὴν ἀποθήκην, τὸ δὲ ἄχυρον κατακαύσει πυρὶ ἀσβέστῳ . Καὶ τοῦτον αὐτὸν τὸν προφήτην συνεκεκλείκει ὁ βασιλεὺς ὑμῶν Ἡρώδης εἰς φυλακήν. καὶ γενεσίων ἡμέρας τελουμένης, ὀρχουμένης τῆς ἐξαδελφῆς αὐτοῦ εὐαρέστως αὐτῷ, εἶπεν αὐτῇ αἰτήσασθαι ὃ ἐὰν βούληται. Καὶ ἡ μήτηρ τῆς παιδὸς ὑπέβαλεν αὐτῇ αἰτήσασθαι τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου τοῦ ἐν τῇ φυλακῇ· καὶ αἰτησάσης ἔπεμψε καὶ ἐπὶ πίνακι ἐνεχθῆναι τὴν κεφαλὴν Ἰωάννου ἐκέλευσε . Διὸ καὶ ὁ ἡμέτερος Χριστὸς εἰρήκει ἐπὶ γῆς τότε τοῖς λέγουσι πρὸ τοῦ Χριστοῦ Ἡλίαν δεῖν ἐλθεῖν· Ἡλίας μὲν ἐλεύσεται καὶ ἀποκαταστήσει πάντα· λέγω δὲ ὑμῖν ὅτι Ἡλίας ἤδη ἦλθε, καὶ οὐκ ἐπέγνωσαν αὐτόν, ἀλλ᾿ ἐποίησαν αὐτῷ ὅσα ἠθέλησαν. Καὶ γέγραπται ὅτι Τότε συνῆκαν οἱ μαθηταὶ ὅτι περὶ Ἰωάννου τοῦ βαπτιστοῦ εἶπεν αὐτοῖς . Καὶ ὁ Τρύφων· Καὶ τοῦτο παράδοξον λέγειν μοι δοκεῖς, ὅτι τὸ ἐν Ἡλίᾳ τοῦ θεοῦ γενόμενον προφητικὸν πνεῦμα καὶ ἐν Ἰωάννῃ γέγονε. Κἀγὼ πρὸς ταῦτα· Οὐ δοκεῖ σοι ἐπὶ Ἰησοῦν, τὸν τοῦ Ναυῆ, τὸν διαδεξάμενον τὴν λαοηγησίαν μετὰ Μωσέα. τὸ αὐτὸ γεγονέναι, ὅτε ἐρρέθη τῷ Μωσεῖ ἐπιθεῖναι τῷ Ἰησοῦ τὰς χεῖρας , εἰπόντος αὐτοῦ τοῦ θεοῦ· Κἀγὼ μεταθήσω ἀπὸ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐν σοὶ ἐπ᾿ αὐτόν ; Κἀκεῖνος· Μάλιστα. Ὡς οὖν, φημί. ἔτι ὄντος τότε ἐν ἀνθρώποις τοῦ Μωσέως, μετέθηκεν ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰησοῦν ὁ θεὸς ἀπὸ τοῦ ἐν Μωσεῖ πνεύματος, οὕτως καὶ ἀπὸ τοῦ Ἡλίου ἐπὶ τὸν Ἰωάννην ἐλθεῖν ὁ θεὸς δυνατὸς ἦν ποιῆσαι. ἵνα, ὥσπερ ὁ Χριστὸς τῇ πρώτῃ παρουσίᾳ ἄδοξος ἐφάνη, οὕτως καὶ τοῦ πνεύματος τοῦ ἐν Ἡλίᾳ πάντοτε καθαρεύοντος, ὡς τοῦ Χριστοῦ. ἄδοξος ἡ πρώτη παρουσία νοηθῇ. Κρυφίᾳ γὰρ χειρὶ ὁ κύριος πολεμεῖν τὸν Ἀμαλὴκ εἴρηται , καὶ ὅτι ἔπεσεν ὁ Ἀμαλὴκ οὐκ ἀρνήσεσθε. Εἰ δὲ ἐν τῇ ἐνδόξῳ παρουσίᾳ τοῦ Χριστοῦ πολεμηθήσεσθαι τὸν Ἀμαλὴκ μόνον λέγεται, ποῖος καρπὸς ἔσται τοῦ λόγου. ὅς φησι· Κρυφίᾳ χειρὶ ὁ θεὸς πολεμεῖ τὸν Ἀμαλὴκ: Νοῆσαι δύνασθε ὅτι κρυφία δύναμις τοῦ θεοῦ γέγονε τῷ σταυρωθέντι Χριστῷ, ὃν καὶ τὰ δαιμόνια φρίσσει καὶ πᾶσαι ἁπλῶς αἱ ἀρχαὶ καὶ ἐξουσίαι τῆς γῆς.
thought_title: Trypho and Justin Discuss Christ and Elijah
pass_a_gloss: And Trypho said, It seems to me that those who say he was a man and was chosen and anointed and became Christ are more persuasive than you who say these things; for we all expect the Christ to be born a man from men, and for Elijah to anoint him when he comes. But if this one is shown to be the Christ, it is necessary to know that he was born a man from men in every way. But since Elijah has not come, I do not declare this one to be him. And I again asked him, Does not the word say through Zechariah that Elijah will come before the great and fearful day of the Lord? And he answered, Yes. If, then, the word compels us to agree that two comings of Christ were prophesied, one in which he will appear suffering and inglorious and unknown, and the other in which he will come glorious and as judge of all, as has been shown in many of the things previously spoken, shall we not think that Elijah's coming was proclaimed by the word of God to be before the fearful and great day, that is, the second coming of Christ? He answered, Yes. And our Lord, I said, handed down this very thing in his teachings, saying that Elijah would come; and we know that this will happen when our Lord Jesus Christ is about to come in glory from heaven, of whom the spirit of God that was in Elijah went before as a herald in John, who was a prophet in your generation, after whom no other prophet appeared among you; who, sitting by the Jordan River, cried out, I baptize you in water for repentance, but the one who is stronger than me is coming, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry; he will baptize you in holy spirit and fire. Whose winnowing fan is in his hand, and he will clear his threshing floor and gather the wheat into the storehouse, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire. And your king Herod had thrown this prophet into prison. And when the day of his birthday was being celebrated, and the daughter of his sister was dancing pleasingly for him, he said to her, Ask for whatever you want. And the girl's mother suggested that she ask for the head of John, who was in prison; and when she asked, he sent and ordered the head of John to be brought on a platter. Therefore, our Christ also said to those who said that Elijah must come before Christ, Elijah will come and restore all things; but I say to you that Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they wanted. And it is written that the disciples then understood that he spoke to them about John the Baptist. And Trypho said, You seem to me to be saying something paradoxical, that the prophetic spirit of God that was in Elijah also came to be in John. And I said to him, Does it not seem to you that the same thing happened with Jesus, the one who succeeded Moses in leadership, when it was said to Moses to lay his hands on Jesus, God saying, Shall I not transfer the spirit that is in you to him? And he said, Yes. As, then, God transferred the spirit from Moses to Jesus while Moses was still alive, so also God was able to bring the spirit from Elijah to John, so that, just as Christ's first coming was inglorious, so also the first coming of the spirit that was always in Elijah might be thought inglorious, just like Christ's. For it is said that the Lord fought against Amalek with a hidden hand, and you will not deny that Amalek fell. But if it is said that Amalek will be fought in the glorious coming of Christ, what is the fruit of the word that says, The Lord fights against Amalek with a hidden hand? Can you see that the hidden power of God came to be in the crucified Christ, whom even the demons fear and all the authorities and powers of the earth?
pass_b_english: Trypho replied, "What those people say seems more persuasive to me: that he was a man, chosen and anointed, and so became the Christ. You say something different. After all, we all expect the Christ to be born a man from men, and we expect Elijah to come and anoint him. If this man is shown to be the Christ, then everyone must know he was born a man from men in every respect. But since Elijah has not come, I cannot accept that this one is he."
I then asked him, "Does not the Scripture say through Zechariah that Elijah will come before the great and terrible day of the Lord?" (Zechariah). He answered, "Yes, it does."

"If, then, the word of God compels us to agree that two comings of Christ were prophesied — one in which he will appear suffering, inglorious, and unknown, and another in which he will come in glory as the judge of all, as has been demonstrated from many passages we have already discussed — must we not understand that the word of God proclaimed Elijah's coming as a precursor to that terrible and great day, that is, the second coming of Christ?" He answered, "Certainly."

"Our Lord, then," I said, "handed down this very teaching: that Elijah would come. And we know this will happen when our Lord Jesus Christ is about to come in glory from heaven. The Spirit of God that was in Elijah went ahead of him as a herald in John, a prophet who arose in your generation; after him, no other prophet appeared among you. John sat by the Jordan River and cried out: 'I baptize you with water for repentance, but one stronger than I is coming, whose sandals I am not worthy to carry; he will baptize you with the Holy Spirit and fire. His winnowing fork is in his hand, and he will clear his threshing floor, gathering his wheat into the barn, but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire'" (Matthew 3:11–12).

"Your king Herod threw this prophet into prison. When Herod's birthday was celebrated, the daughter of his sister danced in a way that pleased him, and he promised to give her whatever she asked. Her mother prompted her to ask for the head of John the Baptist, who was in prison. She asked, and Herod sent an executioner to bring John's head on a platter" (Matthew 14:3–11).

"Therefore, our Christ also said to those who claimed Elijah must come before the Christ: 'Elijah will come and restore all things; but I tell you, Elijah has already come, and they did not recognize him, but did to him whatever they pleased.' And it is written that the disciples then understood he was speaking to them about John the Baptist" (Matthew 17:11–13).
Trypho said, "You seem to me to be saying something paradoxical: that the prophetic Spirit of God that was in Elijah also came to be in John."

I replied, "Does it not seem to you that the same thing happened with Joshua son of Nun, who succeeded Moses in leadership? When God said to Moses, 'Lay your hands on Joshua; shall I not transfer some of the Spirit that is on you to him?' (Numbers 27:18–20)." He answered, "Yes."

"Just as God transferred the Spirit from Moses to Joshua while Moses was still alive, so also God was able to bring the Spirit from Elijah to John. This was so that, just as Christ's first coming was inglorious, the first coming of the Spirit that had always been in Elijah might also be thought inglorious, like Christ's. For it is said, 'The Lord fights against Amalek with a hidden hand,' and you will not deny that Amalek fell (Exodus 17:14). But if Amalek is to be fought only in the glorious coming of Christ, what fruit does the word bear that says, 'The Lord fights against Amalek with a hidden hand'? Can you not see that the hidden power of God came to be in the crucified Christ, whom even the demons dread, and all the authorities and powers of the earth?"

review.notes: The translation accurately captures the nuances of the Greek text, including the distinction between the two comings of Christ and the analogy between Moses/Joshua and Elijah/John. Scripture citations (Zechariah, Matthew, Numbers, Exodus) are correctly identified as allusions or quotations and match the content. Pass A and Pass B are consistent with the Greek source.
